mimic: synthetic data and output control for small populations

mimic-package.Rd

mimic ties together a remote execution workflow for register data on small populations. A researcher never sees the real rows. They develop their script on a synthetic copy, the script is run on the real data in a secure environment, and only output that cannot reveal persons is released.

The workflow

  1. mimic_config() sets the disclosure rules. Defaults are strict.

  2. profile_data() describes the real data. Protection is applied before anything is stored, so the description may leave the secure environment.

  3. mimic() builds a synthetic copy from the description. Level 1 (structure only) is the default.

  4. trial_run() runs the researcher's script on the copy and checks its output with inspect() in advance. In the script, safe_count(), safe_summary() and safe_model() make output that passes, and describe_output() says what each file shows.

  5. real_run() runs it on the real data and returns a safe error report if it fails.

  6. inspect() checks the output and gives a clear approve / needs changes verdict per file; write_report() writes it for the approver.

  7. record_release() keeps what was released in a register, so later output is checked against it.

The rules behind the inspection are also available on their own as the check_*() functions, see checks and check_all().

What mimic protects against

The package is built for an honest researcher who makes mistakes: printing rows, saving identifiers, releasing small cells, saving a fitted model that carries its data, suppressing a cell that the total gives away, or releasing a table that can be subtracted from last month's. Against these it is thorough, and when it cannot tell, it does not approve.

It does not protect against a researcher who deliberately smuggles data out. A script can hide values in what it is allowed to release: in the shape of a figure, in the last digit of a rounded number, in which line it fails, or in a word chosen from its own code for the error message. One bit per run is enough over many runs. No automatic check can rule that out. What helps is outside the package:

  • agreements and trust: access only for known researchers under contract,

  • staff who read the script, not only the output,

  • a limit on the number of runs and on what each run may release,

  • file system permissions and no network in the secure environment. The write guard in real_run() is a safety net, not a sandbox.

Two further limits: figures and Office files are always reviewed by hand, and a level 4 copy from mimic() is built from the real data and is output like any other.

Principles

  • Data protection comes first. When in doubt the package chooses the safe option and warns.

  • No real rows ever leave the secure environment: not in the copy, the description, error messages or logs.

  • Synthesis methods are implemented in the package itself rather than borrowed, so they can be tuned for small populations over time.
